correctness.rationale: Wackenhuth's exact identity writes the autocorrelation evaluation as the nonnegative reduced-diffraction term plus the trivial spectral atom, while the hard-core sign condition gives the matching spatial upper bound. Equality in the density estimate forces the reduced-diffraction integral of the witness transform to vanish. A separate small-support radial test proves that reduced diffraction itself is nonzero for every positive-intensity hard-core packing, so a sharp witness must possess a nontrivial spherical zero. The proof tracks all hypotheses and does not infer an infinite statement from finite computation.

value.rationale: The result is a structural obstruction for sharp hyperbolic linear-programming witnesses: every positive-density equality case requires a genuine spherical-transform zero carrying nonzero reduced diffraction. It rules out an entire natural class of everywhere-positive transforms and supplies the nonperiodic symmetric-space analogue of the zero mechanism behind sharp Euclidean auxiliary functions.
